purpose: Independent exact-byte pre-freeze review of the RT20 retention successor, its checker, and its adjudication response against a candidate-blind semantic-child denominator and all retained RT19 gates. This review does not apply, freeze, seal, integrate, demonstrate, qualify, or release RT20.

scope.decisionRule: PASS requires stable exact subject and transitive-input bytes; every retained gate; a complete independently derived 34-kind/76-semantic-child denominator; 76/76 clean direct and actual-snapshot-root positives; controlled declaration deletions; and zero new blocker.
scope.authoredCheckerRole: Supplemental checker-scope evidence only. Its 24-kind, 58-edge, 65-positive denominator, green mutations, and status fields do not establish that the producer-selected denominator is complete.

reviewerIndependenceAndLineage.predecessorReviewLineageDisclosure: This reviewer authored the exact RT19 independent rejection answered by RT20. That is finding-lineage involvement, not RT20 authorship. Every RT20 conclusion was obtained from fresh exact-byte execution and the candidate-blind denominator rather than from the author's dispositions.

candidateBlindPreparation.statement: The semantic-child oracle, denominator, checklist, retained expectations, and selftests were fixed and hashed before any RT20 path, hash, byte, schema, symbol, or author conclusion was supplied.

exactByteReviewBasis.strictJson: PASS for both JSON subjects under duplicate-key, float, NaN, and Infinity-refusing parsing

verdict.statement: RT20 preserves the retained 55-input, EP8, D9, raw-fixture, lease, purge-root, identity-custody, totality, and deterministic-emission gates. It is rejected because its 24-kind/58-edge/65-positive graph model still does not close the independently derived 34-kind/76-semantic-child denominator. The exact candidate passes only 47/76 direct clean positives and 54/76 actual-snapshot-root clean positives; 29 named rows fail at least one lane.
verdict.effect: RT20 remains rejected and CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED. It must not close Phase 1A, support CD-RT-5, enter E8 or OP6 bindings, or participate in architecture freeze.

blockingFindings.finding: The candidate's CPython referent generalization is incomplete at the exact kinds where it declares exceptions or terminals, and several ordinary runtime kinds are outside its supported positive universe. A code object is an explicit gc.get_referents exception but only co_consts is declared; its name tuples, text metadata, and byte metadata are not visited. A regular-expression pattern is classified as an atomic leaf even though its pattern/group-index metadata are semantic children. Class dictionary and frame-local mapping identities are enumerated through rather than visited as children. Exceptions, tracebacks, weak references, generic aliases, unions, super objects, exact runtime views/iterators, and suspended async-generator drivers are controlled unknown-kind refusals rather than clean supported rows. Consequently the producer's 24-kind/58-edge registry is closed only over its own narrower vocabulary.
blockingFindings.whyAuthoredChecksMissedIt: The authored 65 positive cases and 24 semantic-child rows are derived from the same producer-selected registry. Deleting every declared row proves those declarations are mandatory; it cannot discover a missing type or child. The declared exception registry contains only memoryview, code, and frame and treats code co_consts as complete, while the terminal list silently includes re.Pattern. The general runtime-referents row therefore cannot cover children that gc.get_referents does not return.

decisiveWitnesses.interpretation: A declared atomic leaf retains named metadata and returns clean without visiting it.

decisiveWitnesses.root: exact code object with unique co_filename/co_name/co_qualname values
decisiveWitnesses.interpretation: The code oracle exception traverses only co_consts.
Byte metadata remains outside both gc referents and the explicit exception.

decisiveWitnesses.root: ValueError with a semantic child in args
decisiveWitnesses.interpretation: This is a controlled refusal, not a clean escape, but it demonstrates that an ordinary standard runtime kind is absent from the claimed positive denominator.

requiredRepair: Derive the supported runtime-kind and semantic-child denominator independently from all runtime values reachable through the returned operation graph; publish an explicit one-to-one mapping if candidate and independent row names differ.
Expand the code-object exception to visit constants as objects plus name tuples, text metadata, and byte metadata; reclassify regular-expression patterns and visit their constrained metadata.
Visit class-dictionary and frame-local mapping identities themselves, not only their entries, and close suspended-execution metadata/continuation ownership.

Support the standard runtime kinds currently handled as unknown, or enforce and bind an earlier construction boundary that makes them impossible before the quarantine scan; a self-selected positive subset is insufficient.
Pass all 76 edge-specific direct positives and all 76 actual-snapshot-root positives cleanly. An incidental alternate path to the same identity does not establish the declared child edge.
Add one fail-before-root deletion control for every resulting type and child declaration, retain strong-reference identity custody, and obtain a fresh exact-byte successor review.

rawRegistryDiff.interpretation: Naming differences alone are not the verdict; no complete reviewed one-to-one mapping was supplied, and the behavioral matrix independently demonstrates the omissions.

positiveMatrix.alternatePathCaution: Seven direct failures happened to reach the same child identity elsewhere from the large actual root: pattern-metadata, weakref-callback, generic-alias-origin, generic-alias-args, generic-alias-parameters, union-args, and code-name-tuples. Those incidental hits do not repair their missing direct semantic-child relationship.

currentUnmodifiedSnapshot.interpretation: PASS for the current concrete snapshot only; it is not proof that the traversal algorithm's denominator is complete.

predecessorAndPinLineage.pins: 55 exact inputs; 51 common byte-identical pins; exact four-input RT18-to-RT19 lineage replacement; no common repin

rawFixturesLeasesPurgeAndRoots.purgeAndCustodyInterpretation: storageAndLineage, custodyPolicy, semanticLeaseProtocolV3, and their commitments are byte-identical to RT19; the lease reducers and raw fixture identities were independently recomputed.

selftest.declaredPositiveCases: 65/65 helper and actual root plus 65/65 deletions
selftest.strongIdentityCustody: 20/20 helper and 20/20 actual-root mapping-view lifetime probes

authoredCheckerRegression.interpretation: The authored suite is deterministic and internally green. The rejection is caused by runtime kinds and semantic children absent from that suite's own denominator.

residuals.statement: A successor must close the independently derived semantic-child denominator and receive a fresh exact-byte review.
CD-RT-5 and Phase 1A remain blocked; no product disposition or architecture freeze follows from the retained narrow passes.
No production persistence, transaction, durability, crash recovery, concurrency, fencing, or atomicity behavior is demonstrated.

nonClaims: A green authored checker does not establish a complete semantic-child denominator.
A controlled unknown-kind refusal is preferable to a clean omission, but it is not a clean positive for a claimed supported runtime kind.
An incidental alternate path to a forbidden identity does not prove the named semantic-child edge is implemented.
A clean current concrete snapshot does not prove the traversal algorithm complete.
This review does not apply RT20, update a claim register, accept CD-RT-5, bind E8 or OP6, freeze architecture, or qualify a product release.
